files.role: Cargo package manifest for lance-core. It declares dependency/feature/build surfaces, not executable APIs or evidence that every dependency is used by a specific algorithm.
ranges: Package name is lance-core and description is Lance Columnar Format -- Core Library. Version, edition, authors, license, repository, readme, keywords, categories and minimum Rust version inherit workspace values. They cannot be resolved solely from this manifest.

Dependencies on Arrow array/buffer/data/schema, async-trait, lance-arrow, blake3, bytes and lance-derive inherit workspace constraints. datafusion-common and datafusion-sql are optional workspace dependencies. The manifest establishes availability, not exact usage rationale; source call sites must provide that later.

Workspace dependencies continue with futures, libc, libm, moka, object_store, pin-project, prost, rand, roaring, serde_json, snafu, tempfile, tokio, tokio-util, tracing, twox-hash, url and log. quick_cache is declared with version requirement 0.6 and num_cpus with 1.0 rather than workspace inheritance. These requirements are not resolved lockfile versions. No build dependency or build script is declared here.
Dev dependencies criterion, proptest, rstest, and tokio-stream inherit workspace definitions. Their presence suggests supported testing/benchmark tools, not actual coverage or executed checks.

backtrace is an empty feature, documented disabled by default with zero-sized trace storage; runtime capture additionally requires RUST_BACKTRACE=1. This comment needs confirmation in error.rs before asserting measured overhead. datafusion enables exactly the two optional dep:datafusion-common and dep:datafusion-sql edges. No default feature list is declared.
The cache_keys benchmark disables Cargo's built-in harness. Lints inherit the workspace configuration. No profile overrides, test filtering, or benchmark runtime settings are declared.
files.limits: Exact dependency versions and reasons, feature-conditioned code and backtrace implementation remain pending outside this manifest (rust/lance-core/Cargo.toml:14-65). No Cargo command was run.

files.role: Crate root exporting common modules/errors, public system-column names and lazily initialized Arrow fields, and pure string-to-lineage/system classification functions. No per-dataset mutable state or IO is implemented here.
ranges: SPDX comments and cfg_attr(coverage, feature(coverage_attribute)) enable coverage-only compiler support. extern crate self as lance_core lets derive expansion refer to this crate by its external name. Imports are Arrow DataType/Field (aliased ArrowField) and std::sync::LazyLock.

Public modules are cache, container, datatypes, deepsize, error, levenshtein, traits, utils. The root publicly re-exports ArrowResult, Error, FenceReason, Result and box_error from error. Re-export signatures and variant contracts require error.rs analysis; root visibility alone does not reconstruct them.

Public &str constants are WILDCARD='*' for non-system columns; ROW_ID='_rowid'; ROW_ADDR='_rowaddr'; ROW_OFFSET='_rowoffset'; ROW_LAST_UPDATED_AT_VERSION='_row_last_updated_at_version'; ROW_CREATED_AT_VERSION='_row_created_at_version'. These exact strings form cross-module schema identity, so renaming changes caller matching and column references.

Five public LazyLock<ArrowField> statics use corresponding names, DataType::UInt64, and nullable=true. ROW_ID_FIELD and ROW_ADDR_FIELD comments explain validity bitmaps can be selection vectors; ROW_OFFSET_FIELD stays nullable for compatibility. Creation/update-version fields are also nullable in code. These logical scan fields differ from the persisted non-null hidden-lineage columns required by the schema (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:288-305); do not infer a format contradiction simply from different nullability.

Public i32 reserved IDs are ROW_ID_FIELD_ID=-3, ROW_CREATED_AT_VERSION_FIELD_ID=-4, ROW_LAST_UPDATED_AT_VERSION_FIELD_ID=-5. Comments reserve all negatives, naming -1 unassigned and -2 tombstoned. The prose writes '-3..=-5' informally, not as executable Rust range syntax. Exact numeric identities agree with fragment metadata (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:288-305).

pub fn row_lineage_field_id(column_name: &str) -> Option<i32> is an exact, case-sensitive match: row-ID/created/update names return -3/-4/-5 respectively; every other string, including row address and row offset, returns None. It performs no allocation, IO, mutation, or fallible operation; its only callees are language match/Option construction. The comments identify these as the only negative IDs a physical data-file schema may carry, distinct from fragment field-mapping tombstones. Exact names and reserved numeric values are declared at rust/lance-core/src/lib.rs:22-65.

pub fn is_system_column(column_name: &str) -> bool uses matches! for the five row metadata names, returning false for all other strings including '*'. It is exact/case-sensitive, with no allocation, IO or error path. Comments call all system columns virtual and say user write paths must reject stored names because scanners inject them. This broad prose coexists with the explicit hidden-lineage physical-column facility above; the function itself does not enforce a write restriction or distinguish user fields from internal lineage writes. No unit-test module is present in this file.

files.role: Small dataset abstraction allowing row-taking through lance-core without a concrete lance Dataset dependency. Rust visibility is public, while its documentation explicitly labels it an Internal API.
ranges: License and Dataset Traits module documentation precede Debug, RecordBatch, crate Result and datatypes::Schema imports. Both schema arguments are Lance core Schema, not Arrow Schema.

#[async_trait::async_trait] annotates pub trait DatasetTakeRows: Debug + Send + Sync. Its prose calls it TakeRow and says without the lance trait, but actual identifier and dependency boundary are DatasetTakeRows in lance-core. The HTML warning declares Internal API despite pub visibility. Implementors must satisfy debug formatting and thread-safety bounds; macro-expanded ABI/future signatures require the dependency implementation and are not fabricated here.

fn schema(&self) -> &Schema borrows dataset schema. async fn take_rows(&self, row_ids: &[u64], projection: &Schema) -> Result<RecordBatch> takes internal row IDs and projection, returning one batch or Lance error. No default implementation, row-order/missing-ID policy, cancellation behavior, IO, or tests exist here; those belong to implementors. Changing to physical addresses based solely on u64 representation would violate the documented row-ID meaning.

Arc<dyn DatasetTakeRows> is used by IVF builder/IO interfaces at rust/lance/src/index/vector/ivf/builder.rs:250-250 and rust/lance/src/index/vector/ivf/io.rs:309-309. files.role: Public RowAddress newtype and conversion/formatting helpers for physical fragment-plus-offset addresses. The inner u64 is private. Derived Copy/ordering/hash behavior and arithmetic determine the representation; it is distinct from a stable logical row ID.
ranges: SPDX and Range import precede a doctest showing fragment 5/offset 100 construction, accessors, lossless u64 round trip and '(5, 100)' display. pub struct RowAddress(u64) derives Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash; ordering is the underlying integer order, hence fragment first then offset given its bit layout. No repr(transparent) attribute is declared, so do not promise an external memory ABI.

Public associated constants: FRAGMENT_SIZE:u64=1<<32, TOMBSTONE_FRAG:u32=0xffffffff, TOMBSTONE_ROW:u64=0xffffffffffffffff. new_from_u64(row_addr:u64)->Self wraps without checking. new_from_parts(fragment_id:u32,row_offset:u32)->Self combines fragment in upper 32 bits and offset in lower via shift and OR. Constructors do not reject reserved tombstone values, and cannot return errors.

first_row(fragment_id:u32)->Self delegates to new_from_parts(fragment_id,0). address_range(fragment_id:u32)->Range<u64> returns first_row(fragment)..first_row(fragment+1), half-open. The doctest checks boundaries for fragment 2. Addition fragment_id+1 has no checked_add/guard; callers must avoid u32::MAX, whose next fragment is unrepresentable and may panic with overflow checking or wrap without it. This is a source-derived edge case, not an executed test result.

fragment_id(&self)->u32 shifts right 32; row_offset(&self)->u32 truncates low 32. From<RowAddress> for u64 and From<u64> for RowAddress are lossless raw conversions with no validation and no allocation. Changing the packing changes the interpretation of raw physical-address values even if the From conversions still round-trip losslessly.

Debug::fmt(&self,f:&mut std::fmt::Formatter)->std::fmt::Result delegates to Display through write!. Display::fmt(&self,f:&mut Formatter<'_>)->fmt::Result writes '(fragment_id, row_offset)' using the accessors. No logging occurs: output goes to the supplied formatter, and formatting errors propagate as fmt::Result.

Private cfg(test) module imports the parent items. test_row_address checks raw 0x0000_0001_0000_0002 decodes 1/2, address_range(3).start, a 7/8 round trip and Debug '(1, 2)'. Doctests cover further Display and range-end assertions. Neither shown test exercises u32::MAX range overflow or constructor rejection because constructors do not reject. Tests were read but not run; no measured duration is claimed.
files.limits: Local callees are new_from_parts, first_row, From conversion, accessors and write!/formatting (rust/lance-core/src/utils/address.rs:33-89). Repository-wide callers remain to be indexed during row-address/fragment analysis. No unsafe block, shared mutation or async operation occurs in this file. The reserved maximum-fragment boundary must be considered before using address_range with arbitrary u32 input (rust/lance-core/src/utils/address.rs:27-56).

files.role: Public deterministic blob-sidecar object-store path formatter with two private unit tests. It constructs a path value and does not read/write a blob or generate IDs.
ranges: SPDX header and object_store::path::Path import; no environment/config or global mutable state.

pub fn blob_path(base:&Path,data_file_key:&str,blob_id:u32)->Path reverses all 32 ID bits, formats exactly 32 binary digits followed by .blob, then joins base.clone(), data_file_key, and filename. Base is usually the data directory and key is expected to be the data-file stem, but the function neither strips an extension nor validates that expectation. Callees are u32::reverse_bits, format!, Path clone/join. It allocates formatted/path values, performs no IO, and returns no Result. Reverse_bits obfuscates/scatters sequential prefixes; it is reversible, not encryption.

Private cfg(test) module and test_blob_path_formatting use base/deadbeef with ID 2 and assert exact base/deadbeef/01000000000000000000000000000000.blob output. This fixes bit width, reversal and suffix behavior.

test_blob_path_scattered_prefixes_for_sequential_ids compares IDs 1 and 2, asserts distinct paths, and exact prefixes 1000... versus 0100... for their 32-bit reversed forms. It does not exercise max/zero IDs, empty stems or backend IO. Tests are source-inspected, not executed.
